data.title: Race Condition
data.tagline: A race condition occurs when the ordering of concurrent operations changes the final result.
data.learningOutcome: You can use repeated concurrent runs and timing evidence to identify a race and distinguish one pass from a stable fix.
data.description: Two requests can read and issue the last coupon at nearly the same time, so the read-write order decides whether overselling occurs. Race conditions are broader than data races; request ordering, file state, or event timing can also race, and one passing test does not prove absence.

learning.assumes: You know two requests can access the same state at nearly the same time.
learning.outcome: You can use repeated concurrent runs and timing evidence to identify a race and distinguish one pass from a stable fix.

distinctions.label: Lock
distinctions.explanation: A Race Condition is the defect caused by concurrent execution order; a Lock enforces mutual exclusion to eliminate race conditions.

explanation.title: Problem and key mechanism
explanation.text: Both requests start from one coupon, and different read-write interleavings sometimes issue two; have the concurrent test record each read and write's request ID, value, and time so timing evidence returns to the same run.

explanation.title: Verify stability across repeated runs
explanation.text: After an atomic update or correctly scoped lock, repeated runs yield one success and stock 0. This does not prove every race is gone.

explanation.title: A second scenario: avatar management
explanation.text: If a user uploads a new avatar and immediately cancels it, different upload and delete completion orders can make the avatar reappear. Record the timing and repeat the test to verify the final state always follows the last action.

data.boundary: Race conditions are broader than data races: any concurrent ordering that changes the result can race. A detector finds some unsynchronized memory access, but one clean report or passing run cannot prove absence.

lessonPractice.title: Coupon overselling happens only occasionally under high concurrency. What best gathers race evidence?

options.label: Repeat the same concurrent run and record request IDs and timing for every read and write
options.feedback: Correct. A race depends on interleaving, so repeated concurrent runs and correlated logs reveal why outcomes vary.

options.label: Run once serially and treat a normal result as proof that no race exists
options.feedback: A serial run avoids the competing timing, and one success cannot prove concurrent stability.

options.label: Hide the oversell message and let users retry until one succeeds
options.feedback: Hiding the symptom neither fixes shared state nor provides timing evidence.

data.agentPrompt: Create a repeatable concurrent test for the last coupon so two requests claim from the same initial state. Record request IDs, read values, writes, and timing. Reproduce the race, then fix it with an atomic update or correctly scoped lock. Repeat the run and verify exactly one success and remaining stock 0 every time; do not treat one pass as proof.
